overview: Ahto City is a floating kolto city on Manaan, documented across KOTOR · KOTOR II. Ahto City floats on Manaan's seas as the kolto trade hub where Selkath neutrality law governed Jedi and Sith access during the Jedi Civil War.
history:
Ahto City began as a floating kolto city anchor on Manaan, positioned where water, ore, hyperspace lanes, or sacred geography forced travelers to stop. Ahto City grew where Manaan's resources—water, ore, kyber, or trade lanes—forced travelers to stop, creating a floating kolto city that outlasted first founders. Early survey maps from the Old Republic era list Ahto City as a mandatory customs point for sector governors and Jedi exploration teams. Films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, TOR, and Sith Empire narratives all treat Ahto City as more than scenery—it is a decision point.

Ancient and pre-Republic layers beneath Ahto City include buried fortresses, Rakatan relics, and Sith ward-stones that still disrupt modern sensors. Pre-Republic and Sith-era layers beneath Ahto City include ward-stones, Rakatan markers, and Massassi masonry that modern engineers still discover during repaving. High Republic pathfinders logged Ahto City as a waypoint during the Great Hyperspace Rush, leaving beacon towers that later wars repurposed as artillery spotters. Local archives recovered from Manaan suggest Ahto City once governed trade policy for entire subsectors before centralization on Coruscant.

In the modern era, Ahto City expanded through prefab districts, orbital elevators, and refugee camps that fused multiple species into a single urban rhythm. Clone Wars, Imperial occupation, and New Republic rebuilding each added districts to Ahto City; Mandalorian and Ahsoka-era storylines treat it as a live operational hub. Mandalorian-era bounties and Ahsoka-era investigations repeatedly lead back to Ahto City because its ports lack the scrutiny of Core World bureaucracy. New Republic planners studied Ahto City as a template for rebuilding settlements after the Imperial collapse, citing both its failures and its innovations.

Ahto City has been invaded, liberated, blockaded, and rebuilt more times than most planetary capitals, making its streets a palimpsest of battle damage. Battle dossiers from KOTOR sieges, TOR planetary incursions, and Galactic Civil War raids mark Ahto City as strategically contested on Manaan. Clone Wars dossiers mark Ahto City as strategically vital; Imperial Era governors exploited that same geography to punish rebellious populations. KOTOR-era records and TOR-era campaign logs show earlier iterations of the same struggle—control of Ahto City meant control of Manaan.
significance:
The economy of Ahto City runs on layered industries: docking fees, black-market mediation, sacred tourism, factory output, or casino finance depending on the era. Ahto City's economy mixes legal trade with shadow finance—dock fees, kolto or tibanna exports, scavenging, or casino revenue depending on era and governor. Trade guilds from the Techno Union to the Mining Guild filed competing claims on Ahto City infrastructure during the late Republic. Post-war reconstruction funds often bypass Ahto City officially while flowing through its shadow banks—an open secret among Bothan analysts.

Cultural life in Ahto City mixes planetary tradition with imported habits from every species that ever missed a connection and stayed. Markets, cantinas, and temples in Ahto City blend Manaan native ritual with offworld imports, producing music and cuisine that signal rebel safe houses to trained eyes. Music, food, and festival calendars in Ahto City are used by rebels to signal safe houses and by Imperials to track dissident networks. Jedi historians note that some of the galaxy's quietest acts of mercy—evacuations, forged transit papers, hidden healers—were organized in Ahto City back alleys.

Ahto City influences galactic history disproportionately because leaders, smugglers, and prophets treat it as neutral ground until it suddenly is not. Treaties, betrayals, and superweapon strikes linked to Ahto City altered fleet movements across the Old Republic through Sequel Era conflicts. Scenes set in Ahto City across the saga often mark turning points: treaties signed, betrayals exposed, or the first shot of a regional war. Settlement planners across the Rim still cite Ahto City when arguing for open ports versus fortified capitals—a debate renewed after every occupation.
